newsitem.title: UK: Guinness, GrandMet open door to proposals.
newsitem.headline: Guinness, GrandMet open door to proposals.

text.p: Alcoholic beverage company Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc said Wednesday they were open to proposals from Bernard Arnault, chairman of LVMH Moet Hennessey Louis Vuitton, who is opposing a merger of the two groups.

"We have made it clear to Mr. Arnault that we are, of course, open to any proposals provided that they create additional value for our shareholders beyond our existing proposal and that this is fairly shared between them," said GrandMet and Guinness in a joint statement.

"Accordingly, at our meeting today, we asked Mr. Arnault to detail in writing his specific proposals so that we can evaluate them against these critiria. He has agreed to do this," said the statement.
The statement followed a meeting at LVMH's head office in Paris by Guinness Chairman Tony Greener, GrandMet Chairman George Bull and Arnault.

It was the first meeting held with Arnault, who is a Guinness board member and its largest shareholder with a 14.2 percent stake, since Guinness and GrandMet announced their planned 24 billion-pound ($39.8 billion) merger May 12.
Since then, Arnault has spent more than 8 billion francs ($1.4 billion) to build up a 6.4 percent holding in Grand Met in an apparent attempt to block the merger outright.
A 10 percent stake would allow him to call an extraordinary meeting of GrandMet shareholders and try to win enough of them over to his argument.

Arnault wants to involve his Moet Hennessy beverage division in a three-way alliance in spirits. Some analysts speculate this may be achieved by selling it to GMG Brands, the name given to the merged GrandMet/Guinness group, for a price estimated at as much as $1 billion.
